title: Song of Solomon Bible Quiz - Chapter 2
description: Ten questions on Song of Solomon 2: the rose of Sharon, the banner of love, the voice of the turtledove, and the little foxes.

questions.text: How does the speaker describe herself in the opening verse of this chapter?
questions.explanation: She says, "I am a rose of Sharon, a lily of the valleys."

answers.text: A dove of the mountains and a fawn of the field
A rose of Sharon and a lily of the valleys
A vine in blossom and a green fig
A cedar of Lebanon and a fir

questions.text: To which tree does the speaker compare her beloved among the sons?
questions.explanation: She says, "As the apple tree among the trees of the wood, so is my beloved among the sons," and his fruit was sweet to her taste.

answers.text: The fig tree
The cedar
The palm tree
The apple tree

questions.text: What is the beloved's banner over the speaker when he brings her to the banquet hall?
questions.explanation: She says, "He brought me to the banquet hall. His banner over me is love."

answers.text: Love
Peace
Joy
Gold

questions.text: With what does the speaker ask to be strengthened and refreshed, because she is faint with love?
questions.explanation: She says, "Strengthen me with raisins, refresh me with apples, for I am faint with love."

answers.text: Bread and wine
Honey and milk
Raisins and apples
Figs and pomegranates

questions.text: What does the speaker make the daughters of Jerusalem promise about love?
questions.explanation: She adjures them by the roes and the hinds of the field not to stir up nor awaken love until it so desires.

answers.text: To sing of her beloved's love in all the streets
Not to stir up nor awaken love until it so desires
To tell her beloved she is faint with love
To praise her beloved's love much more than wine

questions.text: Where does the beloved stand as he looks in at the windows?
questions.explanation: She says her beloved is like a roe or a young deer, and behold, he stands behind their wall, looking in at the windows, glancing through the lattice.

answers.text: On the mountains of Bether
At the door of the banquet hall
In the shadow of the apple tree
Behind their wall

questions.text: When the beloved says "Rise up, my love... and come away," what reason does he give about the seasons?
questions.explanation: He says, "For behold, the winter is past. The rain is over and gone," and the flowers appear on the earth.

answers.text: The winter is past and the rain is over and gone
The summer harvest has begun
The day is cool and the shadows flee
The first rains have come on the land

questions.text: What does the beloved ask of his dove in the clefts of the rock?
questions.explanation: He says, "Let me see your face, let me hear your voice, for your voice is sweet and your face is lovely."

answers.text: To fly to the mountains of Bether
To hide until the shadows flee
To let him see her face and hear her voice
To come down to the vineyards

questions.text: What is to be caught because the vineyards are in blossom?
questions.explanation: The verse says, "Catch for us the foxes, the little foxes that plunder the vineyards, for our vineyards are in blossom."

answers.text: The little foxes that plunder the vineyards
The birds that eat the grapes
The young deer on the hills
The snakes among the vines

questions.text: Complete the speaker's words: "My beloved is mine, and I am his. He browses among the..."
questions.explanation: She says, "My beloved is mine, and I am his. He browses among the lilies."

answers.text: vineyards
mountains
fig trees
lilies
